summary_hint: Card authorization by {cardholder}, {card_brand} ...{last4}, up to {authorized_amount} for {charge_purpose}, {one_time/recurring}, dated {authorization_date}.

typed_core.name: merchant_or_lender_name
typed_core.why: identity — who is authorized to charge (flattened from entity)

typed_core.name: borrower_or_customer_name
typed_core.why: identity — the borrower this fee ties to (flattened from person)

typed_core.name: cardholder_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose card (may differ from borrower); flattened from person

typed_core.name: billing_address
typed_core.why: PII — cardholder billing address (flattened from address)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Billing address is cardholder PII — extract verbatim; the snapshot masks it

typed_core.name: card_number_last4_or_token
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — last-4/token identity of the card
typed_core.prompt_hint: Never emit a full card number; reduce to last-4 or the printed token

typed_core.name: expiration_month_year
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — card expiry; disambiguates the card

typed_core.name: authorized_amount_or_maximum
typed_core.why: processor — the cap the borrower authorized

typed_core.name: charge_description_or_purpose
typed_core.why: processor — what the charge is for (appraisal, credit fee)

typed_core.name: authorization_expiration_or_cancel_terms
typed_core.why: processor — how long the authorization stands

typed_core.name: loan_number_property_or_invoice
typed_core.why: identity — links the charge to the loan/property

typed_core.name: charged_amount
typed_core.why: processor — what was actually charged, if the receipt half is present

rejected.name: cvv_cvc_cid_present_on_source
rejected.reason: TECHNICAL — security routing flag, not a fact; never persist the code

rejected.name: cvv_storage_prohibited
rejected.reason: TECHNICAL — security control, not extractable data

encoding_variations: Card is stated as last-4, a tokenized PAN, or (dangerously) a full PAN — always reduce to last-4/token; never persist a full PAN even if printed.
Amount may be an exact charge or a 'not to exceed' maximum — authorized_amount_or_maximum vs charged_amount disambiguate authorization from settlement.
Card brand may be a word ('Visa') or inferable from the BIN — keep the stated brand verbatim.

open_questions.q: Two-in-one authorization + receipt. Some forms carry both the authorization (top) and the settled charge (bottom).
options: two amount fields as designed (authorized_amount_or_maximum + charged_amount)
open_questions.recommendation: keep both fields; flag only if receipts routinely arrive separately GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): keep BOTH amount fields (authorized + charged) — one document carrying both.

open_questions.q: expiration_month_year retention. Card expiry is restricted data with little downstream use once the charge clears.
open_questions.recommendation: register and keep — dropping to catch-all would store it unmasked, which is worse GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): register and keep card expiry (dropping to catch-all would store it unmasked).

open_questions.q: Is this document even needed post-charge? A processor mostly needs proof the fee was paid.
options: keep as its own doc type
open_questions.recommendation: consider whether charged_amount/transaction_status overlap with Evidence of Payment (068)

notes: Assumes one document per extraction — the pipeline does not split multi-document PDFs today (LP-439). Revisit if splitting is added.

No rules today, so no rule floor. This form authorizes a lender/vendor to charge a borrower's card (typically for an appraisal or credit-report fee). It is PII-dense — card number, billing address, expiry — and carries a hard security constraint: the CVV/CVC must never be persisted.

PII registrations needed: card_number_last4_or_token (pre_masked true, last-4/token only); billing_address (pre_masked false, raw address; snapshot masks); expiration_month_year (restricted card data, pre_masked false). Flag.
authorization_or_transaction_id is restricted; treated as a typed field (reason_class identity, not a _PII_FIELDS entry) and flagged for review.
Prompt hint (doc-level, CRITICAL security): if a CVV/CVC/CID is visible, do NOT extract or persist it. The catalog's cvv_* fields are TECHNICAL routing flags, not data to store.
